key_insight: Quantum classifiers do not help uniformly on real image data; their performance depends strongly on whether the input representation geometry aligns with the quantum model’s inductive bias.
engineering_relevance: For practical quantum machine learning pipelines, the main design lever is not just the quantum classifier architecture but choosing classical features whose geometry is compatible with the quantum feature space.
method: Use classical feature extractors for natural images to isolate the effect of the quantum classifier.
Vary data scale and supervision strength to study generalization under different training conditions.
Analyze representation geometry and kernel alignment to identify feature spaces that match quantum inductive biases.
evidence_signal: The study evaluates quantum classifiers on classical visual benchmarks using powerful classical feature representations, showing that effectiveness changes significantly with input geometry and alignment.
watch_item: Reported gains may not transfer if the classical representation is poorly aligned with the quantum feature space, so encoding choice is a critical implementation constraint.
paper_title: Representation Geometry and Inductive Biases in Quantum Classifiers across Classical Visual Benchmarks
